Primary nutrition database backend for future PHP, web, and AI integrations.
The user-facing workbook is separated into fact tables, dimensions, calculated outputs, controls, and quality checks.
Food Log is the primary consumption fact table; each row represents one consumed food record.
Micronutrients, Amino Acids, and Other Nutrients are one-to-one child fact tables linked by Entry ID.
Food Database is the master food dimension linked by immutable Food ID.
Daily Summary and Deficiency Tracker are calculated reporting layers; they should never be manually edited.
Nutrient Dictionary — canonical keys, display labels, categories, units, target behaviour, and active flags.
Lists — controlled values for meals, units, sources, statuses, target types, and central thresholds.
Data Quality — duplicate key, orphan record, missing field, and invalid value monitoring.
System Guide — architecture, relationships, and API operating rules.
Food Database.Food ID  →  Food Log.Food ID
Food Log.Entry ID  →  Micronutrients.Entry ID / Amino Acids.Entry ID / Other Nutrients.Entry ID
Nutrient Dictionary.Nutrient Key  →  Nutrition Targets.Nutrient Key / Deficiency Tracker.Nutrient Key
Treat Food Log and Food Database as append-only database tables; avoid deleting historical records.
Food ID and Entry ID must be unique and immutable. Future PHP writes should use UUIDs.
Use ISO-compatible timestamps and preserve the User ID on every fact record.
Never sort a single column inside a database table; sort or filter the complete row range.
Enter personal target values only in Nutrition Targets. Do not hardcode targets in formulas.
Critical, Low, Good, and Excellent thresholds are centralized in Lists so reporting logic is maintainable.
Upper limits are optional; excess values are flagged only when a nutrient has an upper limit.
Fact sheets are provisioned for 50,000 rows and use lookup-driven formulas against the food master.
The summary layer uses dynamic arrays, LET, FILTER, UNIQUE, SORT, MAP, LAMBDA, XLOOKUP, INDEX, and MATCH.
